interactions.note: Only Total Cover blocks targeting. Three-Quarters Cover and a creature in the line don't. Area spells aren't refused (R-10). This now also covers a healing spell on an ally (Healing Word).
If one chosen target is behind Total Cover, the whole cast is refused before anything is paid.

interactions.with: Hold Person, Cure Wounds, Healing Word, Mage Armor
interactions.note: The caster can choose themself, including for a save spell where the caster is a valid Humanoid target and rolls the save.

interactions.with: Sleep (Sphere, 'of your choice'), Thunderwave (Cube, each creature), Burning Hands (Cone) — R-16
interactions.note: The engine works out the area from the scene. A caller's list only narrows the choice for 'of your choice' spells and never adds a creature outside the area.

interactions.with: Hold Person vs Beast or Fey (2024 Goblin Warrior); Spare the Dying vs a creature above 0 HP; Mage Armor vs an armored creature (R-15)
interactions.note: Each of these is an invalid target: the spell is cast, nothing happens, and no save is rolled. The engine refuses Spare the Dying outright instead.

interactions.with: Action economy: one slot spell per turn; the action
interactions.note: A slot spent on an invalid target still spends the action and still counts as the turn's slot spell.
The player sees only a 'succeeds' save line, and no dice are rolled.
Target kind comes from the spell's description and is a refusal (the R-15 note).

abuse.case: Probing a creature's type by casting Hold Person at it (an invalid target must look like a successful save)
abuse.reason: The player sees only a successful save, and no die is rolled.

abuse.case: Getting the slot back by casting at an invalid target
abuse.reason: The slot and the action are both spent.

abuse.case: (new) Casting at an invalid target so it doesn't count as the turn's slot spell, then casting a second slot spell
abuse.reason: The second slot spell is refused cleanly.

abuse.case: Naming a creature behind Total Cover as a heal target
abuse.reason: The clear-path rule covers every chosen target, allies included.

abuse.case: Leaving creatures off the list to spare them from an 'each creature' area
abuse.reason: The engine finds the creatures in the Cube itself (R-16).

output.summary: This is the second pass for this unit. It adds 13 tests in tests/srd/test_spells.py, following R-15 and R-16: 10 green and 3 red. The tests cover Light on an object; Total Cover blocking a heal on an ally; Hold Person on the Humanoid caster; Sleep's 'of your choice' narrowing; Thunderwave working out its Cube through the session with no names; and Hold Person on a Beast or a Fey goblin (no roll, slot and action spent, still counts as the turn's slot spell). The 3 red tests show the same defect: the engine refuses Spare the Dying on a creature above 0 HP, where R-15 makes that an invalid target (cast, nothing happens, the caster is told it did nothing, no slot). Clauses 6 and 7, and the Hostile exclusion in clause 3, are out of scope. I added one new cheat to the abuse catalogue. Lint and format are clean.
